intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene on chromosome 12q13.

paragraphs.text: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a complex limb malformation that affects the central rays of the autopod (Ugur and Tolun, 2008). It is characterized by absence of the central digital rays, a deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits (Gul and Oktenli, 2002). Most familial cases of SHFM are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner (Gul and Oktenli, 2002). SHFM6 is the autosomal recessive form.

checks.evidence_quote: Split-Hand/Foot Malformation (SHFM) is a complex limb malformation affecting the central rays of the autopod.

checks.claim: SHFM is characterized by absence of the central digital rays, a deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits.
checks.evidence_quote: Split hand and foot malformation syndrome (SHFM) is characterized by the absence of the central digital rays, deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits.

Mufti and Wood (1987) also considered autosomal recessive inheritance likely in their family.

paragraphs.text: Zlotogora and Nubani (1989) raised the possibility of a rare autosomal recessive form of SHFM. They also discussed an alternative 2-locus model, in which a dominant SHFM mutation is controlled by a gene at another locus and a dominant mutation at that controlling locus causes nonpenetrance. Gul and Oktenli (2002) discussed both autosomal recessive inheritance and a 2-locus model for their inbred kindred.

paragraphs.text: Ugur and Tolun (2008) found homozygous WNT10B mutation in a consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM, but inheritance in this family appeared complex (see Molecular Genetics). Blattner et al. (2010) found a homozygous WNT10B mutation in a patient with sporadic SHFM whose heterozygous relatives were unaffected. They concluded that sporadic SHFM is not always a dominant trait and may show recessive inheritance. In that case the recurrence risk is 25% for sibs and very low for the offspring of patients, unless there is consanguinity.

paragraphs.text: By homozygosity mapping in a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM, Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13, with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47. Linkage analysis excluded 4 of the 5 known SHFM loci. At the TP63 locus (SHFM4), most affected individuals carried a rare insertion variant (rs34201045) in the alternate promoter used to transcribe the N-terminally truncated p63 isotype.

paragraphs.text: In a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM, Ugur and Tolun (2008) used a candidate gene approach within the 12q13 linkage region and identified a homozygous missense mutation in the WNT10B gene (R332W). The mutation was present in all affected individuals except the 1 with atypical SHFM. It was also present in 1 asymptomatic female. The authors proposed either that a second locus contributes to the SHFM phenotype or that a suppressor locus prevented the trait from appearing in the nonpenetrant female. They described this as the first reported WNT10B mutation in the pathogenesis of limb development and the first recessive mutation in SHFM.

paragraphs.text: Blattner et al. (2010) examined the WNT10B gene in a patient with sporadic SHFM. They identified a homozygous 4-bp duplication that was predicted to result in a premature termination codon. Nine heterozygous relatives had no sign of SHFM. The authors recommended that patients with sporadic SHFM be tested for WNT10B mutations to determine recurrence risk.

paragraphs.text: In an Indian girl with SHFM, sparse hair, and interrupted eyebrows, Kantaputra et al. (2018) identified a homozygous 3-bp deletion in the WNT10B gene (c.695_697delACA), predicted to cause an in-frame deletion of asn232 (N232del). Protein modeling suggested that deleting this single amino acid at a critical position would severely affect protein structure and function. The authors suggested that the deletion would likely shorten the protein's lifetime and prevent it from binding its receptors and other ligands.

paragraphs.text: In a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM, Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified a homozygous arg332-to-trp (R332W) mutation in the WNT10B gene. The mutation was found by candidate gene analysis within a locus mapped by homozygosity mapping to 12q13.11-q13 (maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47). It was present in all affected individuals except 1 with an atypical, mild phenotype. It was also present in 1 asymptomatic female, which the authors explained by a possible second contributing locus or a suppressor locus.
